cauldron.excerpt: three blessed drops were obtained of the grace of Inspiration. And she put Gwion Bach the son of Gwreang of Llanfair in Caereinion, in Powys, to stir the cauldron, and a blind man named Morda to kindle the fire beneath it, and she charged them that they should not suffer it to cease boiling for the space of a year and a day. And she herself, according to the books of the astronomers, and in planetary hours, gathered every day of all charm-bearing herbs. And one day, towards the end of the year, as Caridwen was culling plants and making incantations, it chanced that three drops of the charmed liquor flew out of the cauldron and fell upon the finger of Gwion Bach. And by reason of their great heat he put his finger to his mouth, and the instant he put those marvel-working drops into his mouth,

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Ceridwen keeps a cauldron boiling to create three drops of inspiration for her son. Gwion receives the drops by accident, gains foresight, and flees; the tale then turns his flight into a sequence of transformations.

narrativeBlocks.title: The drops change Gwion's knowledge
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Guest translation; whitespace normalized): “three blessed drops were obtained of the grace of Inspiration. And she put Gwion Bach the son of Gwreang of Llanfair in Caereinion, in Powys, to stir the cauldron, and a blind man named Morda to kindle the fire beneath it, and she charged them that they should not suffer it to cease boiling for the space of a year and a day. And she herself, according to the books of the astronomers, and in planetary hours, gathered every day of all charm-bearing herbs. And one day, towards the end of the year, as Caridwen was culling plants and making incantations, it chanced that three drops of the charmed liquor flew out of the cauldron and fell upon the finger of Gwion Bach. And by reason of their great heat he put his finger to his mouth, and the instant he put those marvel-working drops into his mouth,”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: The source links poetic inspiration to a specific magical episode. Keep this account in the Mabinogion's Taliesin tale rather than treating it as the origin story of every Welsh bard.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: The Mabinogion is a later translated collection of Welsh tales. This passage is evidence for the tale as transmitted in Guest's edition, not an eyewitness record of an ancient poet's life.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Track what the drops change first—Gwion's knowledge—and then notice how the chase changes bodies and forms.
